_comment: Extra files for File -> Build Game... to pack. You probably do not need this.
_how_the_exporter_decides: Building a game packs ONLY the assets the game refers to - never everything sitting in assets/. The exporter reads every .oscene file and packs each file they name, plus textures/missing.bmp, which the engine loads by name. Everything else stays on your machine: reference art, asset packs bought for a later level, half-finished sprites. That is on purpose. A folder beside a game is something a player can open, and shipping what you did not mean to is how unannounced content and other people's licensed art get out.
_when_you_need_this_file: Exactly one case. A script that builds a path while it runs - LoadTexture("textures/enemies/" + kind + ".png") - refers to a file that NO scene mentions, so the exporter cannot know about it and the exported game will draw the magenta missing-texture square instead. List those files here.
_format: Each entry is a virtual path, the same short form the rest of the engine uses. A file packs that one file. A FOLDER packs everything inside it, at any depth, except script source. Delete the examples and add your own.
